title: Burst ledger drift across regions resulting in tenant starvation and emergency remedial rollout
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Several customers in eu-west and us-east observed sudden token-level 429s and degraded latency during a high-traffic window (2026-03-02 16:00-18:30 UTC). Root cause appears to be an accounting divergence in the reserved-pool burst ledger caused by replication race between regional ledger writers and the global reconciler. The autoscaler reacted to the perceived headroom shortfall by aggressively scaling down warm nodes, which amplified the customer impact. This ticket captures the investigation, mitigations performed, and the long-term fixes being reviewed.
reproduction_steps: Simulate concurrent burst debits for the same tenant from two regions with network partition (iptables drop) between replication leaders
Force one region's ledger write to be delayed >30s and then allow it to commit while the other region has already consumed headroom
Observe reconciler snapshot applied concurrently and confirm double-deduction scenario where a stale delta overwrites a newer balance
Trigger autoscaler with standard safety thresholds and verify scale-down decisions based on stale metrics
impact_summary: Three paying tenants experienced sustained request throttling for 60-150 minutes with visible product degradation. Incident triggered two customer escalations (Account IDs redacted in comments) and an on-call pages. Business impact: measurable SLA violations for Dedicated customers during peak window.

2026-03-02 16:12 UTC: Autoscaler initiates rapid scale-down in multiple reserved pools after headroom metrics fall below threshold

mitigations_and_workarounds: Immediate: Issued emergency 'reserve_topup' to affected tenants to restore headroom and unblock requests
Immediate: Temporarily set autoscaler.min_active_replicas=1 for affected pools to prevent further cold-downs
Hotfix: Deployed reconciler guard that rejects older ledger deltas using per-tenant vector timestamp checks (canary in eu-west)
Customer comms: Ops sent status updates and offered committed credit compensation; Account execs are coordinating follow-up
root_cause_analysis_summary: The dedicated reserved-pool ledger is replicated asynchronously across regional leaders. Under a short-lived network partition plus concurrent burst consumption, two region writers created deltas based on diverging preimages. The reconciler applied a stale snapshot because it lacked a proper causal ordering mechanism, causing the global balance to be set lower than the true available burst. The autoscaler uses this global headroom signal without a quorum-aware safety filter, which caused premature scale-downs and exacerbated starvation.
long_term_fixes: Implement CRDT-style burst ledger (operational transform) or attach monotonic vector clocks to ledger deltas to enforce causal reconciliation
Make autoscaler decision logic quorum-aware: require confirmation from 2/3 regional writers for large headroom drops before triggering mass scale-down
Add a synthetic safety buffer to headroom signal during cross-region reconciles and network anomaly windows
Improve observability: add 'ledger_conflict_rate' and per-tenant reconciliation events to Runtime Console dashboards
proposed_implementation_notes: Prefer vector-clock approach for minimal semantics change. Reconciler change will include delta validation and out-of-order rejection. Requires migration plan: reconciler must tolerate mixed mode for up to 48 hours. Autoscaler patch to gate scale-downs behind a confirmed_headroom flag and introduce fast-path emergency_topup if confirmed_headroom < threshold and pending_reconcile=true.
rollout_plan: Canary patch reconciler in eu-west with 5% of tenant traffic for 6h
Monitor ledger_conflict_rate and headroom_stability for 12h, abort on regressions
Deploy autoscaler gate with feature flag; enable only after reconciler is stable
Post-deploy: run reconciliation validation job and runbook to sweep any remaining negative balances
runbook_actions_for_oncall: Step 1: If tenant 429s spike, run 'reserved_pool_topup' with justification and note in incident log
Step 2: Verify regional replication health: kubectl get statefulset/ledger-writer -n dedicated and check pod restarts
Step 3: If replication lag > 15s, set autoscaler.disable_scale_down=true for affected pools and open emergency PR
Step 4: Trigger reconciler dry-run with --validate-only to preview ledger corrections before apply
Step 5: After mitigation, restore autoscaler flags and capture full incident snapshot (logs + heap profiles)
